summary: No Nvidia filing, release, guidance change or export-rule ruling dated 29 or 30 October turned up, and the SEC filing list shows nothing new for the window. The only company-specific items are an unverified aggregator note on the CEO's comments about a Singapore customer under US investigation (an old story) and the Justice Department's questions on the Hugging Face deal (reported 28 October, only questions so far), neither of which changes the research. The capex read-through sits inside the research scenarios, so the research target (12m) of 262.70 stands; I could not reopen the big-four primary sources myself.

items.headline: Alphabet Q3 disappoints investors; Big Tech AI spending questioned; Nasdaq down 1.38%, NVDA closed 213.66 (down 0.8%)
items.why: Price-move story with no Nvidia-specific cause. The capex-digestion tail is the risk the research already sizes; the big-four 2026 guides netting to about 730 billion versus 732.5 billion (your check, not re-verified by me) is a 0.3 percent change, inside scenarios, and no company gave a numeric 2027 figure.

items.headline: Reuters: US Justice Department asking how Nvidia's 12.9 billion Hugging Face purchase would affect AI competition (follow-up coverage 29 Oct)
items.why: First dated 28 October, one day before the window, so it does not count today. Only questions, no action; deal is about 0.25 percent of market value and expected to close in the first half of 2027. What I could not size: any lasting limit on Nvidia's future acquisitions or software distribution.

items.headline: Jensen Huang tells Bloomberg dealings with Singapore customer Megaspeed were ordinary business; Nvidia says earlier export-evasion claims were 'debunked'
items.why: Only seen on an aggregator page. The underlying New York Times story is from October 2025 (checked). The research already assumes no China data center revenue in the guide; an actual enforcement action on Nvidia would be new and was not found.
